# Pkl 0.32.0 DataSize and Bytes additive Java authority

This fixture is separate from the 255-row DataSize authority in `m2-data-size`. It preserves actual public Java evaluator captures 04–09 and the pinned upstream source/lock snapshots in `oracle-evidence.tar.gz`. `tools/data_size_supplement_fixtures.py` independently pins the archive, member file set, executed Java probe bytes, inputs, JAR, runtime image, source snapshots, complete process protocols, raw channels and two fresh JVM repetitions. Run `python3 tools/data_size_supplement_fixtures.py` for an offline audit. It never starts Java or a Rust candidate. `inputs/05`, `inputs/07`, `inputs/08`, `inputs/09` are exact common string-query candidate inputs; `inputs/06` is a separate public export identity producer input.

Capture04 is retained as an incomplete *wrapper* attempt: its four actual JVMs exited zero and repeated raw files agree, but its wrapper incorrectly retained a 255-row completion condition for 44 rows and saved `complete=false`. Capture05 was acquired fresh with the condition corrected and is the additive 44-row split authority. Its string sessions made 44 calls each (24 successes, 20 ordinary Pkl errors); export sessions made 49 actual calls each, including five traced DataSize repeats (29 successes, 20 errors). Captures07–09 are additional split source-query/export sessions with separate fresh evaluators. Capture06 is a separate two-JVM, 16-public-export-call-per-JVM identity experiment. Each cohort keeps actual errors and full process stdout/stderr as raw bytes. No Java observation counts as a candidate compatibility pass.

Capture05 records `DataSizeUnit` alias, typed and default controls, inherited `ifNonNull`, absent method/property and argument diagnostics, Bytes factory UInt8 boundaries/types and evaluation order. Actual `Bytes.size` from encoded strings returns `0.b`, `1.b`, `999.b`, `1.kb` at 1000 bytes and `1.024.kb` at 1024 bytes. Capture06 records Java public array/DataSize wrapper identity separately from Pkl Bytes language equality. Captures07–09 distinguish query-level unqualified built-in `Bytes(...)`, qualified module method calls and module-source lexical calls when a user method named `Bytes` is declared.

The common candidate boundary is each source-query cohort's ordered module URI/query calls, status, complete UTF-8 stdout/stderr and process protocol. Java error class, exported Java type, DataSize bits/hash/unit, public byte-array reference/equals/hash and wrapper identity are separate producer or public API evidence. They cannot be synthesized by a Rust candidate. Capture04 stays inconclusive for completion. Pkl Binary, broader Bytes and renderer APIs, candidate native/Node/browser comparison, whole language, lifecycle, OS and performance requirements remain open.
